# Logicaffeine

> LOGOS is an English programming language. Write English sentences and get First-Order Logic; write English programs and get running code, a web app, or Rust, C, WASM and RISC-V. Current release: 0.11.0.

## What it is

Logicaffeine is a natural-language compiler with two modes that share one parser.

- **Logic mode** turns English into First-Order Logic (Unicode, LaTeX, ASCII or Kripke form) with neo-Davidsonian event semantics, modal and temporal logic, and every reading of an ambiguous sentence: "Every woman loves a man." comes back with both quantifier scopes.
- **Imperative mode** compiles LOGOS programs: static types, ownership, generics, pattern matching, contracts, modules, tests written in the language (`## Test`, `Expect that …`, `For all` properties), structured concurrency on a seeded, replayable scheduler, and CRDTs for shared state.
- **LGX**, the web framework: a page is one file (`State:`, `Actions:` in English, `View:` HTML, `Style:` CSS) compiled to WebAssembly, and `## Route`s ending in `Serve on port 8080.` are the server.
- **Execution:** a tree-walking interpreter, a register bytecode VM, EXODIA (a copy-and-patch JIT), and ahead-of-time Rust, C, direct WASM and RISC-V backends; `largo emit` writes CUDA, Tenstorrent and other device bundles.
- **Proofs:** a Calculus of Constructions kernel with an independent second checker, SAT solving with DRAT/LRAT certificates, Lean 4 import re-checked by both kernels, and optional Z3 static verification.

A model asked to formalize a sentence guesses one reading; LOGOS parses, so it returns them all, and a proof counts only when the kernel checks it.

## Get started

- Install (Linux, macOS): `curl -fsSL https://logicaffeine.com/install.sh | sh`
- Install (Windows, in PowerShell): `irm https://logicaffeine.com/install.ps1 | iex`
- Pairing with a person, step by step (install, learn the language, start a project, then code, logic, math and hardware): https://logicaffeine.com/agent.txt
- First program, no Rust toolchain needed: `largo new hello && cd hello && largo run --interpret`
- Getting started guide: https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md
- In the browser, no install: https://logicaffeine.com/studio

## Documentation

- Guides: https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/docs/README.md
- Every construct on one page: https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md
- Rust API documentation: https://docs.logicaffeine.com
- Everything in one file for language models: /llms-full.txt
- Machine-readable companions: /errors.json (every diagnostic code with its Socratic explanation) and /examples.json (the runtime-verified example corpus with expected outputs)
- The toolchain is an MCP server: `claude mcp add logos -- largo mcp`

## Main Pages

### / (Homepage)
"Code we can all read. Logic and mathematics built in. Bring your own agent." The agent instructions a person pastes into their coding agent (install largo, read /llms-full.txt, start a project, then code, logic, math and hardware with the released largo), copied in one click. Below them, a mini Studio: a LOGOS web page in the Studio's editor beside its live preview, and a Logic, a Math and a Hardware example to run.

### /studio
Interactive three-panel IDE with Logic, Code, Math, Hardware and Web modes:
- File browser with example files
- Live editor with syntax highlighting
- Context-sensitive output (FOL formulas, AST trees, REPL, proofs)
Free to use, no account required.

### /learn
A roadmap for learning First-Order Logic, one lesson at a time:
- Era 1: First Steps (Introduction, Syllogistic Logic, Fallacies)
- Era 2: Building Blocks (Propositional Logic, Proofs)
- Era 3: Expanding Horizons (Quantificational, Modal, Deontic, Belief Logic)
- Era 4: Mastery (Ethics, Metalogic, History, Deviant Logic, Philosophy)
Each lesson gives two examples and one question, with a hint after a wrong answer and optional extra practice.

### /guide
The interactive syntax guide; every example runs in place:
- LOGOS syntax and grammar
- Lexicon configuration
- First-Order Logic concepts
- Code examples with Run/Copy/Reset

### /contact
Contact the team. LOGOS is open source under the MIT License. The page holds the install commands, a form that reaches the team, and the FAQ.

### /crates
The crates published to crates.io, each described in its own manifest's words:
- logicaffeine-base: Foundation types for Logicaffeine: arenas, string interning, spans, and exact integers, decimals, quantities, money, dates and UUIDs
- logicaffeine-cli: largo — the LOGOS build tool: projects, builds, tests, serving, proofs, and the package registry
- logicaffeine-compile: The LOGOS compiler: type checking, the optimizer, the interpreter and bytecode VM, and the Rust, C, WASM, RISC-V, CUDA and hardware backends
- logicaffeine-data: LOGOS runtime values, collections, wire format and CRDTs, shared by native and WASM builds
- logicaffeine-forge: The machine-code layer of the LOGOS copy-and-patch JIT: W^X executable memory, build-time stencils, a register-allocating x86-64 backend
- logicaffeine-jit: Native execution tier for the LOGOS bytecode VM: hot functions and loops tier up to x86-64 machine code
- logicaffeine-kernel: Calculus of Constructions proof kernel with inductive types, universes, quotients, a second checker and Lean 4 import
- logicaffeine-language: The LOGOS front end: English sentences to first-order logic, and the parser for LOGOS programs and LGX pages
- logicaffeine-lexicon: The English vocabulary behind LOGOS: verb, noun and adjective metadata for build-time lookup tables, plus an optional runtime JSON index
- logicaffeine-lsp: The LOGOS language server (LSP): diagnostics, completion, hover, navigation and refactoring for .lg files, literate .md files and LGX pages
- logicaffeine-proof: Kernel-checked proof search and tactics, certified SAT/CDCL with DRAT/LRAT output, and a number-theory and cryptanalysis library
- logicaffeine-runtime: Deterministic, replayable concurrency runtime for the LOGOS interpreter and VM: task scheduler, channels, Select, timers, seed and trace
- logicaffeine-system: Platform IO, networking, HTTP serving, persistence, and post-quantum crypto (Keccak/SHA-3, ChaCha20-Poly1305, ML-KEM, ML-DSA) for LOGOS
- logicaffeine-tv: Translation validation for LOGOS: a symbolic encoder of the source, checked with Z3 against the tree-walking interpreter per program
- logicaffeine-verify: Z3-based static verification and model checking for Logicaffeine

### /roadmap
Development roadmap with 13 milestones:
1. Core Transpiler (Complete)
2. Web Platform (Complete)
3. Imperative Language (Complete)
4. Type System (Complete)
5. Concurrency & Actors (Complete)

11. Translation Validation (In Progress)
12. Quantum Backend (Planned)
13. Silicon (In Progress)

### /benchmarks
Live benchmark results with full methodology: 35 programs across 11 languages (C, C++, Rust, Zig, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Nim, LOGOS), the certified-solver-vs-the-field comparison (Z3, Kissat, SaDiCaL, CaDiCaL, CryptoMiniSat), and the wire-codec head-to-head (Protobuf, Cap'n Proto, MessagePack, bincode, postcard, CBOR, Arrow, JSON). Every number links to raw JSON and reproducible harnesses.

### /registry
Package registry for community-contributed logic modules. Search, browse, and publish packages with GitHub authentication.

### /news
Release notes, tutorials, and announcements — one article per release with engineering deep-dives (each article is statically served at /news/<slug>; the full list is in /sitemap.xml).

### /privacy
Privacy policy.

### /terms
Terms of service.

## Technical Details

### Supported Logic Systems
- Classical propositional logic
- First-order predicate logic
- Modal logic (necessity, possibility)
- Deontic logic (obligation, permission)
- Epistemic logic (belief, knowledge)
- Temporal logic (past, future, always)

### Architecture
- **Frontend**: Dioxus 0.7 (Rust) compiled to WebAssembly; content pages are statically prerendered for crawlers
- **Backend**: Rust with arena-allocated AST, symbol interning
- **Logic pipeline**: Input → Lexer → Parser → AST → Transpiler → FOL Output
- **Imperative pipeline**: five execution tiers — tree-walking interpreter, register bytecode VM, copy-and-patch JIT, AOT-to-Rust, and a direct WASM backend
- **Proof Engine**: pure-Rust certified prover (SAT/CDCL, GF(2)/GF(p) algebraic routes, SR symmetry proofs) checked by a CoC proof kernel; Z3 powers the optional native static-verification tier

### Performance
Measured by the open benchmark suite (35 programs x 11 languages, results at /benchmarks):
- LOGOS release binaries: 4.16x geometric-mean speedup vs C — faster than Rust (1.05x), Zig (1.09x), and C++ (0.99x) on the same suite
- The certified solver beats Z3, Kissat, CaDiCaL, and CryptoMiniSat by orders of magnitude on structured UNSAT families (pigeonhole, Tseitin parity, mod-p counting)
- The wire codec produces the smallest encoding on every fair workload vs Protobuf, Cap'n Proto, MessagePack, bincode, postcard, and CBOR

### Lexicon System
Vocabulary database (lexicon.json) defining:
- Verbs with Vendler class and transitivity
- Nouns with animacy, gender, and number
- Adjectives with intersective/subsective properties
- 2000+ vocabulary entries

## Technical Details

### Supported Logic Systems
- Classical propositional logic
- First-order predicate logic
- Modal logic (necessity, possibility)
- Deontic logic (obligation, permission)
- Epistemic logic (belief, knowledge)
- Temporal logic (past, future, always)

### Architecture
- **Frontend**: Dioxus 0.7 (Rust) compiled to WebAssembly; content pages are statically prerendered for crawlers
- **Engine**: Rust, with an arena-allocated AST and symbol interning; the same engine runs natively and in the browser as WebAssembly
- **Logic pipeline**: Input → Lexer → Parser → AST → Transpiler → FOL Output
- **Imperative pipeline**: a tree-walking interpreter, a register bytecode VM, a copy-and-patch JIT, and ahead-of-time Rust, C, direct WASM and RISC-V backends
- **Proof Engine**: pure-Rust certified prover (SAT/CDCL, GF(2)/GF(p) algebraic routes, SR symmetry proofs) checked by a CoC proof kernel; Z3 powers the optional native static-verification tier

### Performance
Measured by the open benchmark suite (35 programs x 11 languages, results at /benchmarks):
- LOGOS release binaries: 4.16x geometric-mean speedup vs C — faster than Rust (1.05x), Zig (1.09x), and C++ (0.99x) on the same suite
- The certified solver beats Z3, Kissat, CaDiCaL, and CryptoMiniSat by orders of magnitude on structured UNSAT families (pigeonhole, Tseitin parity, mod-p counting)
- The wire codec produces the smallest encoding on every fair workload vs Protobuf, Cap'n Proto, MessagePack, bincode, postcard, and CBOR

### Lexicon System
Vocabulary database (lexicon.json) defining:
- Verbs with Vendler class and transitivity
- Nouns with animacy, gender, and number
- Adjectives with intersective/subsective properties
